description.narrative: TradeMark Africa's Rwanda Country Programme works to reduce trade costs and deepen Rwanda's integration into regional and global markets, building on over fifteen years of engagement since 2010 along the Northern and Central Corridors, the country's primary trade routes connecting it to the Port of Mombasa and the broader Great Lakes region. The Programme combines physical connectivity investments, including One Stop Border Posts at Ruzizi and Kagitumba, port infrastructure on Lake Kivu, and road upgrades on key corridor links, with a comprehensive digital trade systems agenda spanning the Electronic Single Window, the Trade Logistics Information Pipeline (TLIP), cargo tracking, e-certification, and AI-enhanced trade portal services. Complementing this infrastructure and systems work, the Programme supports Rwanda's alignment with AfCFTA, WTO, and regional trade frameworks, upgrades national standards and sanitary and phytosanitary capacity at the Rwanda Standards Board, and runs targeted interventions to expand market access for MSMEs, including agri-food SME coaching in international food safety standards, with a deliberate focus on formalising and financing women, youth, and persons with disabilities through the Women-in-Trade model and cooperative linkages to regional buyers.
Kigali is the capital city of Rwanda

provider-org.narrative: Denmark - Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Danida

receiver-org.narrative: TradeMark Africa (TMA) is a leading Aid-for-Trade organisation founded in 2010 to grow intra-African trade, increase Africa’s share in global trade, and make trade more pro-poor and sustainable. We operate on a not-for-profit basis, funded by a strong coalition of development partners including Canada, Denmark, the European Union, Finland, France, the Gates Foundation, Ireland, the Mastercard Foundation, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom. TMA works closely with regional and continental institutions, national governments, the private sector, and civil society to unlock trade and investment opportunities across the continent.

title.narrative: Market Access and Business Competitiveness in Rwanda
Value of exports for supported firms in Rwanda

description.narrative: Value in tonnes of exports for supported firms in Rwanda

comment.narrative: Since July 2025, USD 1.4m worth of exports have been recorded.

title.narrative: Jobs created, sustained and improved as a result of TMA projects

description.narrative: Jobs created, sustained and improved as a result of TMA projects

comment.narrative: Onboard and empower 100 additional SMEs with technical skills for market entry with a target of 2500 Youth in Work.
2,500 jobs supported in Q3 (Y25/26), total youth employment tracked is 26,000.
23,500 youth in work, with 4,500 primary youth in work and 19,100 youth employed by the 5,000 supported firms. Of these 43% are women.

title.narrative: Value(USD) of investments leveraged from external sources to support TMA programs

comment.narrative: $2.3 million leveraged for SMEs financing through support in development of bankable business plans and proposals that are them subjected to different funding mechanisms.

title.narrative: Volume of exports handled through the Rubavu port

comment.narrative: 1,400 tonnes of cargo handled per month through the Port of Rubavu in FY 25/26, supported by a logistics hub with 5,000 m² of bonded warehouses and cold storage. This represents about 70% of its capacity, with full capacity estimated at ~2,000 tonnes/day. On an annualised basis, this implies operations of about 510,000 tonnes/year at current operations against it’s designed capacity of about 700,000 tonnes/year. In total, 53,000 tonnes of cargo was handled through the Rubavu Port from April 2025 to March 2026.

title.narrative: Number of TMA supported private sector enterprises that have obtained certification with quality institution(s) in meeting minimum product standards

comment.narrative: 58 MSMEs in horticulture, dairy, and meat value chains were certified; 16 in Global GAP, 15 with the S-Mark, 7 with HACCP, 2 with SMETA and 18 registered with RICA, positioning them to access regional and global markets. 2,200 businesses formalised their operations, positioning them to access finance, attain certifications, and integrate into structured and high-value supply chains.

title.narrative: Percentage reduction in product interdceptions among supported enterprises.

comment.narrative: 45% reduction in product interceptions among supported enterprises demonstrating strengthened regulatory capacity in the meat sector. 37 private meat inspectors licensed by RICA out of the 40 young professionals trained to continue contributing to improved food safety standards and job creation within the sector.

title.narrative: Value of exports from firms supported by TMA

comment.narrative: $ 3.6 million export value generated from 4 international trade fairs in Germany, Middle East (Dubai), China and Spain with 24 enterprises participating. A woman-led exporter in Rwanda completed its first-ever shipment of a 20-foot container of Hass avocados to the UAE.

title.narrative: Value of goods traded by traders receiving direct support from TMA programs

comment.narrative: Cumulative $9.7 million in new exports generated from women and youth-led SMEs, with $ 3.7 million of it generated from trade fair deals in Germany, Middle East (Dubai), China and Spain by 55 participating enterprises. A woman-led exporter in Rwanda completed its first-ever shipment of a 20-foot container of Hass avocados to the UAE.
